author: Rahul kp
title: Forward vs Reverse
simple_words: Forward charge: the seller pays GST to the government. Reverse charge: the buyer pays it.

definitions.meaning: The supplier collects GST from the recipient on the invoice and deposits it with the government. This is the normal rule.
The recipient pays GST directly to the government instead of the supplier. It applies only to supplies the law specifically notifies.

key_points: Under ==forward charge== the supplier is liable to pay the tax.
Under ==reverse charge== the recipient is liable, but only for notified supplies.
!!RCM tax cannot be paid from the ITC balance!!; it is paid through the cash ledger.
If the supplier is unregistered, the recipient raises a self-invoice for the RCM supply.

insight.text: The tax is the same in both cases; only the person who deposits it with the government changes.
insight.punchline: Law decides who pays, not you!

memory_trick.explanation: Reverse and Receiver both start with Re, so under RCM the Receiver pays. Otherwise (Forward), the Seller pays.

steps: Check if supply is under RCM
Claim ITC on RCM tax if eligible
exam_tip: Under RCM, pay the tax in cash first. Claim ITC afterwards only if the input is eligible and used for business.

doubt.question: Does RCM mean no GST is charged on the supply?
doubt.answer: No. GST is still payable at the same rate. The supplier does not collect it; the recipient pays it directly to the government.

mistakes.wrong: Paying RCM tax by using the ITC balance
mistakes.right: RCM tax is paid through the cash ledger; ITC can be claimed later if the input is eligible.

mistakes.wrong: Applying RCM to every purchase from an unregistered supplier
mistakes.right: RCM applies only where the law notifies that supply or class of recipient.

mistakes.wrong: Saying the recipient never gets ITC on RCM tax
mistakes.right: After paying the tax, the recipient can claim ITC if the input is eligible and used for business.
